text:
sam.sales: FYI — new POC with a regulated client. They want a Private/VPC deployment but have strict network controls: they need fixed egress IPs for their firewall, and they insist the source IP used for requests to downstream systems is traceable back to the originating internal user. Also want a short firewall snippet we can hand to their netops.

anya.sol: Quick clarifying q: will traffic originate from their VPC to our service (they call our endpoint), or do we need to call their downstream services on their behalf? That changes whether they need our egress IPs or vice versa.

sam.sales: They will call our inference endpoint in their VPC via PrivateLink interface endpoint. Downstream systems are internal to their VPC and need to see the original client IP for auditing.

leo.net: Two realistic approaches: (1) PrivateLink + static EIPs for our outbound (customer allowlists our EIPs). This is easiest operationally for us but means their firewall sees our EIP(s), not the original client IP. (2) Transit/VPN (L3) so we SNAT-preserve via routed path — the destination sees original client IPs because routing doesn't NAT. Option 2 is heavier.

maria.sec: From a security perspective, if they require per-user attribution we need either tcp-level src IP preservation or strong application-level identity (mTLS client certs, per-user JWTs). If they accept mTLS/jwt, we can avoid L3 complexity. Need to capture what their auditors require.

ben.ae: Customer compliance is very strict: firewall logs must show originating internal CIDR -> external destination. They said app-level tokens aren't enough for their auditors. So they want true src-IP preservation.

anya.sol: Practical middle-ground: we can offer a lightweight on-prem sidecar (container) or EC2 in their VPC that terminates PrivateLink traffic and forwards to internal services while preserving X-Forwarded-For. That way their internal services see the original client IP in a header they control. Caveat: their firewall appliances may not log headers — need to confirm.

leo.net: Example firewall allowlist (if we provide fixed EIPs):

```
# CUSTOMER FIREWALL - allowlist example
allow proto tcp from any to 18.197.45.101/32 port 443 comment "redwood-egress-1"
allow proto tcp from any to 18.197.45.102/32 port 443 comment "redwood-egress-2"
```

sam.sales: Do we guarantee those EIPs for PrivateLink? Or only for Dedicated / reserved capacity?

leo.net: We can promise fixed EIPs for Dedicated Private stack (reserved pool). For standard hosted PrivateLink endpoints, EIPs are not guaranteed — they're managed by us and can change. If they need strict allowlist and contractual guarantee, recommend Dedicated + EIP reservation (add-on).

maria.sec: Also consider advising them on SNI/TLS-inspect: if their appliances intercept TLS, they will break mTLS unless we adjust. Recommend mTLS end-to-end or use IP allowlist instead of FQDN to avoid SNI dependency.

ben.ae: Can we provide a short cost delta now to inform procurement? They asked if EIP reservation is a big add-on.

anya.sol: Rough ballpark for POC: reserve 2 EIPs + 5TB transfer = EIP reservation $350/month + bandwidth @ our private rate (I'll fetch exact). If they do L3 VPN setup instead, there's setup overhead (engineering time) but no EIP add-on. I'll confirm numbers with billing.

leo.net: If they want L3 (Direct Connect/VPN + TGW peering) here's the minimal ops checklist for them:
- Accept BGP or provide managed VPN credentials
- Provide a subnet for our cross-connect if using hosted appliances
- Provide contact + maintenance window for BGP sessions
- Firewall rules: allow inbound from our routed ASN / subnet

# Short sample for L3 inbound allow on their firewall:
```
# allow routed traffic from Redwood via TGW/VPN
allow from 10.10.100.0/24 to 10.0.0.0/16 proto any comment "redwood-vpn-peer"
```

maria.sec: Action item: sam, get their compliance doc excerpt that states why tcp src IP is mandatory. That will determine whether we push for L3. If it's purely auditing, an alternative is to enable detailed request-level logging with customer-anchored user IDs + mTLS.

ben.ae: I'll request a quick netops workshop — need to align on PrivateLink vs TGW, EIP commitment, and TLS strategy.

ops-bot: Reminder: attach the private deployment network runbook and standard contract clause for reserved EIPs to the calendar invite — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privatedeploy-network

anya.sol: One more option to propose: PrivateLink + customer-run connector (we provide container) deployed in their VPC that accepts PrivateLink traffic and forwards internally without SNAT. That preserves original IPs in internal logs and keeps our infra out of their CIDR. Slight operational lift for customer but often hits the auditor sweet spot.

sam.sales: Good list. Please prepare: (1) a short email with 2 recommended architectures (PrivateLink+EIPs vs L3/TGW) and pros/cons, (2) firewall snippets for both approaches, (3) ballpark pricing for EIP reservation and transfer. Need to send to customer before lunch PT.

anya.sol: Will do — drafting now and will ping billing. @leo.net can you sanity-check the firewall snippets and add any AWS-specific notes (ENI, interface endpoint security group rules)?

leo.net: Will do. For customer-facing SG example: allow outbound HTTPS from their app subnet to the interface endpoint DNS name and allow inbound from the endpoint SG to the connector EC2/container. I'll paste sample SG rules in the email.

sam.sales: Thanks all. I'll stand up the call if needed after they review the email. :thumbsup:
